newsitem.title: USA: Anaheim, Calif., prepares $500 mln Disney deal.
newsitem.headline: Anaheim, Calif., prepares $500 mln Disney deal.

text.p: Anaheim, Calif., will come to market with a $500 million bond deal in February that will put Walt Disney Co's $1.4 billion expansion in southern California on the fast track, officials said Friday.

The city is in the final process of sizing the lease revenue bond deal, Anaheim Finance Director William Sweeney said. The city plans to price the bonds in the first week of February and to close the deal about a week later, he said.
Proceeds will fund improvements to areas surrounding the Disneyland resort and to the city's convention center.
Disney financial adviser Jon Schotz said he expected "smooth sailing" when the $500 million deal comes to market.

Getting to market, however, has been a long and difficult process. For years, city officials have been in discussions with Disney about expanding. Critics warned that Anaheim's budget would be at risk if the city took part in the deal.
In October, Anaheim's city council backed Disney's expansion plan. In November, voters approved a local tax measure that will help to support the $500 million bond deal.
This week, the city faced a new challenge when Moody's Investors Service Inc downgraded its debt.
